title: NSDR for a High-Stress Day
description: Your ring shows two hours or more of stillness with a raised heart rate today and very little calm time. A longer NSDR session can help the body come back down.

all.label: 120+ minutes of stillness with a raised heart rate today (phone-estimated)
under 30 minutes of calm recovery today (phone-estimated)

conditional.question: Your ring shows a long stretch of raised heart rate with little calm time today. Does that fit how your day has gone?

actions.frequency: Once, on the day this triggers
actions.timing: Early to mid afternoon, or whenever you can lie down undisturbed
actions.details: Follow a guided NSDR recording lying down with eyes closed. It is designed to shift the body toward parasympathetic rest and restore alertness without sleeping.

actions.action: Hold off on adding extra stimulation
actions.frequency: Once, on the day this triggers
actions.details: Skip extra caffeine and heavy news or social media for the rest of the afternoon so the session is not immediately undone.

benefits: Gives a concrete recovery step on a day with a long stretch of arousal
Short NSDR sessions are associated with lower stress and improved alertness
science: NSDR protocols such as Yoga Nidra have been associated with reduced stress and better recovery, and Huberman recommends them as a way to restore calm and energy during the day. This rule is experimental: the stress estimate is computed on your phone from heart rate relative to your resting rate while still, and has not been validated as a measure of stress.
contraindications: Do not use in place of medical care if you feel unwell
The estimate can be raised by caffeine, illness, or dehydration as well as stress
Avoid lying down for NSDR if you are drowsy and need to drive or operate machinery

learning_resources.title: Non-Sleep Deep Rest (NSDR) — Huberman Lab official page

evidence_metadata.scientific_rationale: A long stretch of raised heart rate during stillness with almost no calm time suggests the day has had little autonomic recovery. Requiring both signals separates a stressful day from one that just has a single tense stretch.

evidence_for_protocol.notes: NSDR / Yoga Nidra is a standard Huberman Lab recommendation for restoring calm and energy, and is the same tool used by the existing recovery-deficit protocols.

evidence_for_trigger.notes: The 120 and 30 minute cutoffs are first-pass guesses, untuned on a full day of real ring data. Treat as unvalidated until tuned.

expected_effect.short_term: Lower subjective tension and a calmer heart rate after the session.
expected_effect.long_term: Not outcome-tested for this specific trigger.
